review_notes: I read the whole file: the main reduction theorem and the short wrapper theorem. I also checked the other files in LeanPool/Feige for repeated proof blocks. The only repetition I found is `hc_nonneg` and `hc_le_one` at lines 106–115 of Reduction.lean. They re-prove `sharpConstant_nonneg` and `sharpConstant_le_one`, which already exist in Constants.lean (lines 44 and 48). Constants.lean is imported publicly. The `pow_le_one₀` argument in the `hc_le_one` block (Reduction.lean 109–115) matches the one in `sharpConstant_le_one` (Constants.lean 48–52). The fix is to call the existing lemmas, which needs no new shared lemma. The duplicated reasoning is also a few lines of routine positivity and `pow_le_one₀`. That is too small, and too much a case of reusing existing API, to count as repeated proof machinery under this rubric, so I did not report it. The other pieces are each used once: the measurability, integrability and independence of the shifted variables, the mean computation, the sum identity, and the bad-event complement argument. The wrapper theorem is thin. I found no other nontrivial repeated reasoning.
